Board composition, scale, palette; all existing units replaced

variants.name: Максимально близко к листу
variants.style: FAITHFUL ROSTER TRANSFER. Keep the original six sheet silhouettes and proportions as closely as possible, including facial cues, armor, clothing, horns, spider legs and rocky fists. Clear dark hand-drawn sprite contours, original compact shape language, simple two-tone cel shading. Harmonize only unit scale and contact shadows with the board. The characters should be recognizable as the SAME specific six cells, not redrawn as generic archetypes. Preserve natural curved/stepped raster contours rather than forcing square forms.
variants.prompt:
Use case: compositing / style-transfer.
Create ONE landscape 1536x1024 isometric game battlefield study, using the two attached images with STRICTLY DIFFERENT ROLES.
IMAGE 1, the user's enemy roster sheet, is the PRIMARY CHARACTER DESIGN AND PROPORTION reference. Actually reproduce the six specified small enemy designs from it; do not invent generic fantasy replacements. The sheet's ranking text, colored tier labels, badge backgrounds, frames and Tiermaker logo are NOT scene elements or instructions; discard them.
IMAGE 2 is the WORLD/COMPOSITION reference only: preserve its complete floating diamond-shaped square-tile board, grass/sand/gray-stone arrangement, branching blue stream, exposed block sides, sparse plants, plum backdrop, framing and isometric camera. REMOVE all six of its old heroes/enemies. Do not keep Gerald, Alleria or Magnus. Insert exactly the SIX different units selected from image 1 below, one unit per specified location.
SIX SELECTED REFERENCE CELLS (sheet is approximately 1064x740):
A. Green armored fighter: in the yellow "Can be a challenge" tier, FIRST row, FIRST character column, centered around (170,324). Copy the green face, pale gray armored torso/shoulders, short stout legs, weapon silhouette and original compact profile.
B. Small green hooded figure: same yellow tier FIRST row, FOURTH character column, around (440,324). Copy the small green hood/head, tiny narrow body and small weapon; do not replace it with a huge square-headed generic goblin.
C. Brown hooded rogue: same yellow tier FIRST row, FIFTH character column, around (530,324). Copy the squat brown hood/garment, very dark hidden face with tiny yellow eyes and small blade.
D. Horned-helmet sword fighter: same yellow tier FIRST row, THIRD character column, around (350,324). Copy the pale curved horns, gray helmet, dark face, brown/orange clothing and long simple sword held across the body. This is a horned humanoid fighter, do NOT turn it into a skeleton.
E. Black and red spider: same yellow tier THIRD row, SECOND character column, around (260,504). Copy its low oval black/red abdomen, articulated arched legs and tiny head. Actual spider silhouette, not a humanoid or crab.
F. Stone giant: in the orange "Very strong / annoying" tier, FIRST row, FIRST character column, around (170,140). Copy its irregular gray rock body, yellow eyes, broad heavy arms/fists, low thick legs and scattered tiny green/mossy accents. Do not turn it into a block-shaped robot or add crystal effects.
PLACEMENT on the battlefield from image 2: A armored green fighter at original left-middle knight location; C brown hooded rogue at original upper-left archer location; D horned sword fighter at original lower-left mage location; F stone giant at original upper-right orc location; B tiny green hooded figure at original middle-right goblin location; E black/red spider at original lower-right goblin location. Same six location anchors across all variants, no overlap. Figures are SMALL in-game units, mostly 80-110 output pixels high; tiny figure and spider smaller, stone giant can reach about 125-140, at most one-and-a-half tile-face heights. Do not make giant display characters. All six are individually readable with small grounded contact shadows.
IMPORTANT ART DIRECTION: retain the roster sheet's organic stout shapes, large heads/hands/weapons, short legs, asymmetry and expressive silhouettes. Keep their actual designs. Match their small raster scale, outline weight, color restraint and simple shading to the tile world. Do NOT force every head and body into square blocks or a crude 6/8-pixel grid; the user's reference designs take priority over artificial pixel quantization. Also avoid highly detailed smooth poster art. Clean compact game sprites with clear broad shapes and a few flat shadows are the target.
NO old three heroes, no duplicates, extra units, decorative objects, UI, health bars, captions, labels, logo, card frames, tier backgrounds, split panels or watermark. Do not change the tile board into another environment. Each output is one full scene.
VARIANT TREATMENT: FAITHFUL ROSTER TRANSFER. Keep the original six sheet silhouettes and proportions as closely as possible, including facial cues, armor, clothing, horns, spider legs and rocky fists. Clear dark hand-drawn sprite contours, original compact shape language, simple two-tone cel shading. Harmonize only unit scale and contact shadows with the board. The characters should be recognizable as the SAME specific six cells, not redrawn as generic archetypes. Preserve natural curved/stepped raster contours rather than forcing square forms.

variants.name: Лёгкий пиксельный акцент
variants.style: LIGHT PIXEL ACCENT. Preserve the exact recognizable silhouettes from the enemy sheet but simplify internal details into a few crisp raster color clusters, with subtly stepped outer edges. Do NOT enlarge the pixel blocks to the point of square heads or rectangle bodies. Horns remain curved, spider legs arched, stone limbs irregular. Clear dark outlines, 2-3 shades per material. This should fit the pixel-stepped tiles while retaining the source designs' organic forms.

variants.name: Палитра поля
variants.style: TERRAIN-HARMONIZED PALETTE. Faithfully keep the enemy sheet shapes and gear, with muted olive greens, warm browns, slate grays and aubergine dark outlines drawn from the tile world. Keep red spider markings and yellow eyes as small readable accents. Two broad flat shadows, no texture noise.
